chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Yunus from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The waiting period (iddah) of the woman who undergoes mu'ararah (mutual consent divorce), khul' (redemption divorce), and khiyar (option of divorce) is the same as the waiting period of the mubtala' (irrevocably divorced) woman, and they observe their waiting period in their husbands' houses.

key_terms.الْمُبَارَأَةِ: Mutual consent divorce where the husband releases the wife from marital bonds.
key_terms.الْمُخَيَّرَةِ: Divorce involving the option (khiyar) of the wife to choose between staying or leaving.
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: Divorce by redemption (khul'), where the wife pays compensation to the husband to end the marriage.
key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: The irrevocably divorced woman, serving as the standard reference for the waiting period.
key_terms.بُيُوتِ أَزْوَاجِهِنَّ: The husbands' houses, the designated place for observing the waiting period.
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death before she can remarry.

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman in khul' or mu'ararah divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the *iddah* (waiting period) for women undergoing *mu'ararah* (mutual separation), *khul'* (redemption), and *khiyar* (option of divorce) mirrors that of the standard revocable divorce. This ruling emphasizes that, unlike widows who may wait in their own homes, these women must remain in their husband's residence (*bayt al-zawj*) to preserve lineage clarity and marital dignity, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence.
